raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Gemma-4 with the FA backend (`--attention-backend fa4`) and the `google/gemma-4-31B-it-assistant` draft (promoted to `FROZEN_KV_MTP`) crashes on the first request with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`.

**This is a latent bug in `FlashAttentionBackend`, not a regression from #42019.** The FA backend never resolved the SWA KV pool for a frozen-KV draft. It stayed hidden because Gemma-4 could not select the FA backend on Hopper: the SM90 FA4 kernel did not support the head dimension 512 of Gemma-4's global-attention layers, so Gemma-4 ran on Triton. #42019 ("Enable Gemma4 FA4 on SM90 with head-dim 512 support") makes `--attention-backend fa4` selectable for Gemma-4 (opt-in; Triton stays the default). That opens the FA backend to the Gemma-4 SWA + frozen-KV MTP draft combination for the first time, and exposes the bug. Without this fix, `--attention-backend fa4` + MTP on Gemma-4 crashes on `main`.

Root cause: the FROZEN_KV_MTP draft has no KV of its own and reads the target's KV, but its `ModelRunner.token_to_kv_pool` is a plain (non-SWA) pool. `FlashAttentionBackend.__init__` derived `use_sliding_window_kv_pool` from that pool, so it was `False` for the draft. Full-pool page-table slots were then never translated to SWA slots, and the smaller SWA buffer was indexed out of bounds.

`flashinfer`, `trtllm_mha` and `aiter` already resolve the SWA pool from the allocator for frozen-KV drafts (`_resolve_swa_kv_pool`). The FA backend was the odd one out.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashattention_backend.py`
- Add `FlashAttentionBackend._resolve_swa_kv_pool`, mirroring the flashinfer/trtllm_mha resolver: use the active pool if it is a `SWAKVPool`; for a draft worker, only FROZEN_KV_MTP falls back to the allocator's SWA pool (other EAGLE drafts keep their own separate pool and still get `None`).
- Store the result in `self._swa_kv_pool`, derive `use_sliding_window_kv_pool` from it, and use it at every place that calls `translate_loc_from_full_to_swa` / reads `full_to_swa_index_mapping` (previously `self.token_to_kv_pool`).
- For every non-frozen-KV case the resolved pool is the same object as before, so behavior is unchanged.

`test/registered/unit/spec/test_resolve_swa_kv_pool.py`
- Register the FA backend resolver in the existing `_RESOLVERS` table.

## Accuracy Tests

The change only selects which pool the page table is translated against; it does not touch kernels or model code, so accuracy with MTP should equal accuracy without it.

Setup: lm-eval GSM8K, 5-shot, chat template, greedy, `max_tokens=4096`, 32 concurrent requests, full test set. 1x H200, `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-block`, `--attention-backend fa4`, server flags as under Speed Tests.

**On `main` + this PR**

| Config | flexible-extract | strict-match | accept length | accept rate | `illegal memory access` in server log |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no speculative decoding | 0.9712 ± 0.0046 | 0.9719 ± 0.0045 | - | - | 0 |
| MTP4 (FROZEN_KV_MTP) | 0.9712 ± 0.0046 | 0.9719 ± 0.0045 | 4.26 | 0.814 | 0 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### 1. Crash reproduction and fix (control vs this PR)

Setup: `main` (`1814ece`, contains #42019) in a fresh venv built from `python/pyproject.toml` (torch 2.14.1, flash-attn-4 4.0.0b34), 1x H200, `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-block` + `google/gemma-4-31B-it-assistant`, `--attention-backend fa4 --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 4 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 5 --disable-radix-cache`, `bench_serving --dataset-name random --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio 0.2 --max-concurrency 8`. Control = `main`, patched = `main` + this commit. One run per cell.

| Cell | main (control) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| MTP4, 8k input, c8 | crash: `illegal memory access`, bench exit 1 | clean, 497 output tok/s, accept len 3.32 (rate 0.58) |
| MTP4, 32k input, c8 | crash: `illegal memory access`, bench exit 1 | clean, 137 output tok/s, accept len 3.41 (rate 0.60) |
| no speculative decoding, 8k, c8 | clean, 305 tok/s | clean, 306 tok/s |

Patched-only cells (no control run), all with 0 `illegal memory access` lines:

| Cell | output tok/s | accept len (rate) |
|---|---|---|
| MTP2, 8k, c8 | 453 | 2.49 (0.74) |
| MTP6, 8k, c8 | 498 | 3.80 (0.46) |
| MTP4, 8k, TP=2, c8 | 539 | 3.37 (0.59) |

Accept length / rate in this section are the mean of the per-batch values printed in the server log (15-20 batches per run, batches with fewer than 2 running requests skipped), so they are approximate. In the crashed control run the accept length was already degenerate (1.20, rate 0.05) before the crash. The no-speculation row shows the non-frozen-KV path is unchanged. Throughput numbers are single runs and only show that the server runs.

### 2. SpeedBench (aiperf, `throughput_8k`) on `main` + this PR

Setup: aiperf `speed_bench_throughput_8k_<category>`, `--endpoint-type chat --streaming`, `--osl 1024`, `ignore_eos`, 80 conversations at concurrency 8 and 320 at concurrency 32, one server per (arm, category) serving both concurrencies (`--max-running-requests 32`, `--context-length 262144`, `--swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.3`, radix cache on). 1x H200, `main` + this PR, one run per cell. Accept length comes from the `/metrics` `spec_verify_calls` deltas around each run; accept rate is `(accept length - 1) / 4` (4 draft steps).

High-entropy category:

| Config | conc | output tok/s | TTFT p50 (ms) | TPOT p50 (ms) | ITL p50 (ms) | accept length | accept rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no speculative decoding | 8 | 261.9 | 4228 | 20.6 | 18.8 | - | - |
| no speculative decoding | 32 | 620.3 | 11643 | 37.8 | 27.9 | - | - |
| MTP4 | 8 | 328.0 | 696 | 15.3 | 25.5 | 2.19 | 0.30 |
| MTP4 | 32 | 733.8 | 6857 | 36.2 | 43.8 | 2.33 | 0.33 |

Low-entropy category:

| Config | conc | output tok/s | TTFT p50 (ms) | TPOT p50 (ms) | ITL p50 (ms) | accept length | accept rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no speculative decoding | 8 | 254.7 | 4198 | 20.8 | 19.0 | - | - |
| no speculative decoding | 32 | 615.4 | 11959 | 37.2 | 27.9 | - | - |
| MTP4 | 8 | 438.7 | 750 | 10.3 | 25.9 | 4.35 | 0.84 |
| MTP4 | 32 | 922.2 | 6553 | 26.7 | 44.5 | 3.49 | 0.62 |

`illegal memory access` lines in the server logs: 0 in all six runs (GSM8K and SpeedBench, MTP4 and no speculative decoding).

Note: the unit test only mocks the model runner and checks which pool the resolver returns, so it does not by itself prove the crash is gone; the end-to-end tables above are the evidence.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (`pre-commit run --files ...` passes on both files)
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (not needed: no user-facing change)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (tables above)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

issue_comments.body:
Hi @BBuf, this fixes a latent bug in `FlashAttentionBackend` that the FA4 backend (#42019) exposes under `FROZEN_KV_MTP` with Gemma-4: the SWA layers looked up KV in the wrong pool. The fix uses `self._swa_kv_pool` instead.

Validated on H200 (1 GPU, `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-block`, `--attention-backend fa4`):
- GSM8K: 0.9712 (no-spec) vs 0.9719 (MTP4), i.e. the two arms score the same
- SpeedBench MTP4 gains over no-spec at c8 and c32, no illegal-memory errors in any run

Could you take a look and add `run-ci` when you get a chance? CI is blocked on `pr-gate` until then.

@HaiShaw, as a CODEOWNER for the attention layer, would you mind reviewing as well? Thanks!
